provenance.frame_count_deviation: requested 30, used 27: smoke 6's committed 30-frame run has no right hand on f_0001..f_0003, so 27 is the full set of right-hand MANO parameters available. The sequence was not padded, duplicated or mirrored to reach 30.
provenance.note: MANO *parameters* only (pose/shape/trans). The 21-joint skeleton is recomputed here by retarget/mano_fk.py from the pkl; smoke 6's own joints_3d is never read.

c1b_status.what_c1b_actually_checks: shape and finiteness only: our numpy MANO forward pass returns (21, 3) finite joints. It does NOT compare them against a reference implementation.
c1b_status.why_it_is_unverified: the committed test opens with pytest.importorskip('smplx'), so it had never executed in the CI venv (runs/.venv-retarget has no smplx). The 3.6e-8 m figure rests on a run this test file cannot reproduce. See commit ae64f8a, which un-broke the test without adding any comparison.
bugs_found_by_ae64f8a: hands_mean is stored flat (45,), one 3-vector per hand-pose joint; the test added it straight to a (15, 3) rotvec block (ValueError: shapes (15,3) (45,)). Fixed with .reshape(15, 3).

Rotation.from_rotvec on a (15, 3) block yields 15 rotations, so as_rotvec() comes back 2-D and the np.concatenate against the flat global_orient failed on dimensionality. Fixed with .reshape(-1), because MANO's pose parameter is one flat 48-vector (global_orient 3, then hand_pose 45).
c1b_status.why_a_real_comparison_is_not_a_one_liner: smplx.MANO expects the npz-style shapedirs/posedirs arrays, but MANO_RIGHT.pkl is a pickled dict, so smplx.create() fails on shapedirs[:, :, :10]. A genuine cross-validation needs the pkl converted to the npz layout first.

retargeting.ref_value: 21-joint MANO targets, wrist-centred, indexed by target_link_human_indices

gauge_fixing.rule: one constant rotation R_g = (mean hand world orientation)^-1 plus the clip's mean in-plane offset (dx, dy), applied to the whole clip. The absorbed yaw is the dominant term: it is what had pushed wrist_rz to 2.71 rad against a +-1.57 rad ctrlrange. z is untouched because the hand's height above the object is physical.
gauge_fixing.physical_meaning: this is a coordinate convention, not a physical change: the hand's pose in the world is unchanged, only the wrist joint angles that represent it are re-referenced. The removed yaw is the global orientation of a hand with no fixed arm, and the removed x/y offset is the arbitrary origin of the floating base.

wrist_anchor.anchor_rule: floating base xyz solved by retarget/base_solve.py against the box's grasp geometry; the per-frame wrist orientation and slide motion are the retargeted clip's own and are not fitted
wrist_anchor.superseded_anchor_rule: single constant translation offset placing the mid-clip retargeted fingertip centroid on the tissue-box proxy TOP face; no per-frame term

search.objective: minimise the closest fingertip-to-box gap over the whole clip, subject to zero hand-geom interpenetration of the box at every frame. The box is not moved; only the hand's base is solved.
search.grasp_axis: x (the box's 120 mm span, frozen in the MJCF)
search.feasibility: no hand geom may interpenetrate the box, and the palm collision plate must stay a full fingertip-pad radius off it, at every frame

base_solve.grasp_tips_note: at the closest-approach frame 2 of 4 fingertips are within 15 mm of the box

constrained_solve.method: temporally coupled solve: alternating projection onto {actuator ctrlrange INTERSECT joint range} and onto the signed velocity band, with a damped Gauss-Newton step between them on the hand world-pose objective (palm frame origin + all four fingertips) using MuJoCo's analytic body Jacobians. No per-frame independent IK.
constrained_solve.objective: sum_t ||hand_world(x_t) - hand_world(x_retargeted)||^2 over the palm frame origin and the four fingertips

hand_world_pose_deviation.definition: how far the constrained solve moved the hand in the world away from the pose the retargeted clip asked for, split into the palm frame (the hand's base pose) and the worst fingertip

fingertips.definition: worst of the four fingertips' ||solved - retargeted|| world positions, per frame

constraints.slide_move_cap_note: per-frame wrist-slide movement from the retargeted command is bounded by cap/sqrt(3) per axis, so the palm frame's world position cannot leave a ball of that radius; the palm frame origin is hand_root + slides exactly

constrained_solve.box_intersection_note: the box is the actuator ctrlrange INTERSECT the joint range; the retargeter commands several finger joints outside both

contact.definition: any contact between a finger/palm geom and the tissue-box proxy geom; contacts against table_slab/pedestal/floor are excluded
contact.superseded_note: C6 (contact_occurred) is superseded per the W6 acceptance (PLAN 2026-10-16): the dual-hand sweep covers the whole table and the structural premise of a single replay's contact proof is gone; A2/A3a carry the contact-nature gate in W6c

penetration.tolerance_rationale: MuJoCo's default solref/solimp lets a resting body sink a small fraction of a millimetre; the measured box-on-pedestal resting sink in this very scene is 2.909e-05 m, so 1e-3 m is ~9x the solver's own resting tolerance and still 3 orders of magnitude below the 40 mm box half-height

servo_winding_tolerance.rule: three-part servo winding tolerance, per finger joint: (1) excess beyond jnt_range <= |forcerange|/kp, (2) at most 3 consecutive control frames (150 ms at 20 Hz), (3) the transient is elastic wind-up: there is a contact torque on that DoF, the actuator is not on its force limit while it happens, and kp*(ctrl-qpos) accounts for the whole non-actuator load on the DoF to 5%. An excursion during saturation is never exempted, and neither is one on a freely drifting joint.

joint_limits.note: the retargeted command is clipped to each actuator's ctrlrange before it is applied; the realised qpos is then checked against the MJCF joint range. mjcf_range_violation_frames is the zero-tolerance evidence (frames where qpos left jnt_range at all); the gate that judges them is servo_winding_tolerance, the user-approved three-part servo winding table. This MJCF gives every finger joint limited=true with stiffness=0, so jnt_range is an assertion the gate checks, not a mechanical stop the solver enforces -- which is exactly why an elastic wind-up can carry qpos past it.

joint_motion.gated_quantity: commanded rate between consecutive control frames, np.diff(ctrl)/0.05, over the warm-start ramp concatenated with the replay

velocity_limit_source.finger: URDF velocity="3.14" on all 16 finger joints
velocity_limit_source.wrist_hinge: free-space measured trackable rate at 20 Hz (ratio >= 0.9)
velocity_limit_source.wrist_slide: free-space measured trackable rate at 20 Hz (ratio >= 0.9)
velocity_limit_source.measured_quantity: commanded rate between consecutive control frames, np.diff(ctrl)/0.05, over the warm-start ramp concatenated with the replay
velocity_limit_source.excludes: the 3.687 rad/s wrist step-response peak is deliberately not the gate: it is what the servo does on a step, not what it can track

joint_motion.velocity_max_rad_s_note: realised qpos rate over all velocity DoFs (both hands plus the box's free joint; only the right hand is commanded), evidence only; it is not the gate

actuators.n_actuators_note: the W6a dual-hand scene carries 44 position servos (two hands); smoke 5 commands the right hand's 22 and leaves the left hand's servos at ctrl 0, which holds it frozen at its initial pose
actuators.ctrl_saturation_rule: any |command - clipped ctrl| > 1e-9 in a frame
actuators.force_saturation_rule: actuator_force on its forcerange bound (1e-6 rel tol)

wrist_reachability.interpretation: a non-empty axes_out_of_range means the retargeted wrist pose cannot be executed by this floating wrist; the replay then clips the command, so the executed trajectory differs from the retargeted one and the executed qpos is gated on the MJCF joint range instead

wrist.ceiling_rationale: physically anchored, same rule as smoke 2: a jump must exceed BOTH 3x the median inter-frame step AND an absolute per-frame ceiling. The ceiling comes from the wrist actuator authority -- force-limited position servos (slides +-45 N, hinges +-6 N m) on a ~0.15 kg hand over a 50 ms control period reach ~0.11 m of single-step travel, so the ceiling is set at 0.05 m (and 0.5 rad on the rotation axes) to keep margin

fingertip_tracking.interpretation: evidence only, not a gate: smoke 6 measured HaMeR's own fingertip error at mean 45.6 px / p90 111.6 px under occluded grasping, so this term inherits that uncertainty and is recorded rather than thresholded

physics_provenance.mjcf_commit_message: p0(w6a-v21): rf/th forcerange hardware alignment — v12 precedent completed
physics_provenance.accounting_rule: every number in this report was produced on scene_sha256 == 29896fe50740, i.e. commit 98c498a. Numbers produced on commit e170b6d (scene_sha256 bc75a8e4e542) belong to the superseded physics and must not be mixed with these.

gate_definition.measured_quantity: mean joint rate over one 20 Hz control period, np.diff(qpos)/0.05 -- an interval average, not the URDF's instantaneous max joint speed
gate_definition.applies_to_dofs_in_code: all 22 qpos DoFs, finger and wrist alike

urdf_velocity_scope.note: every velocity=3.14 attribute sits on a finger joint; the URDF's wrist_joint is type=fixed (the palm root), so the MJCF-only 6-DoF floating wrist has no URDF velocity specification to inherit.

startup_transient.note: reset_scene() seeds the wrist at identity, so interval 0 asks the servo for a step of up to ~1.3 rad in 50 ms. Intervals 1-2 are the servo still catching up to that step. The retargeted trajectory itself never asks for more than 2.05 rad/s after interval 2.

floating_wrist_servo_ceiling.actuators: wrist_rx/ry/rz: position servo kp=14 N m/rad, forcerange +-6 N m
floating_wrist_servo_ceiling.measurement: box lifted 3 m clear in a throwaway model copy, so this is the servo alone and not a contact reaction
floating_wrist_servo_ceiling.tracking_criterion: mean achieved rate >= 0.9x the commanded rate
floating_wrist_servo_ceiling.conclusion: the servo peaks at 3.67 rad/s on a step but only tracks a constant-rate ramp faithfully up to 2.0 rad/s; 3.14 rad/s is a step-transient rate, not a 20 Hz trackable rate.

commanded_pose_probe.method: kinematic only (mj_forward, no dynamics, fingers at the reset pre-curl): box overlap of the commanded configuration
commanded_pose_probe.note: a ~53 mm burial would mean the gauge-fixed retarget output asks for fingers through the box. It does not: the commanded pose overlaps the box by well under a millimetre, so the deep-travel known boundary does not fire on this sequence.

box_contact_force_split.note: R1 sized forcerange for 10 N per fingertip, 40 N summed across the four pads; the peak per-frame total normal force on the box is reported for comparison. C6 counts any finger-or-palm geom, so a palm-only contact satisfies it; the per-geom breakdown records which geoms actually carry the load.

known_boundary_check.verdict: the revision's declared known boundary (commanded interpenetrating finger poses reachable, ~950 N of solver force resolving 53 mm of burial, box possibly flung) did NOT materialise on this sequence
